qa_pairs.instruction: Summarize the management capabilities available for the SAP Portal driver.
qa_pairs.output: The SAP Portal driver supports a full set of management capabilities including starting, stopping, and restarting the driver; viewing version information; using Named Passwords for secure password storage; monitoring health status; performing backups; inspecting cache files; viewing statistics; using the DirXML Command Line utility for scripted management; securing the driver and its data; synchronizing objects; and migrating and resynchronizing data. All of these tasks are documented in the NetIQ Identity Manager Driver Administration Guide.

qa_pairs.instruction: What is the purpose of Named Passwords in the SAP Portal driver?
qa_pairs.output: Named Passwords in the SAP Portal driver provide a secure method for storing passwords associated with the driver, preventing clear‑text exposure and allowing administrators to reference passwords by name rather than embedding them directly in configuration files.

qa_pairs.instruction: Which utility can be used to script management tasks for the SAP Portal driver?
qa_pairs.output: The DirXML Command Line utility can be used to perform management tasks for the SAP Portal driver through scripts.

qa_pairs.instruction: How can an administrator monitor the health status of the SAP Portal driver?
qa_pairs.output: An administrator can monitor the health status of the SAP Portal driver by using the monitoring functions described in the NetIQ Identity Manager Driver Administration Guide, which cover status checks and health reporting for the driver.

qa_pairs.instruction: What common driver management actions are listed for the SAP Portal driver?
qa_pairs.output: Common management actions listed for the SAP Portal driver include starting, stopping, and restarting the driver; viewing driver version information; using Named Passwords; monitoring health status; backing up the driver; inspecting cache files; viewing statistics; using the DirXML Command Line utility; securing the driver and its information; synchronizing objects; and migrating and resynchronizing data.
